method: Public, read-only reconstruction. Sources are the platforms' own skill.md / API docs and the BasedAgents SPEC.md, all fetched 2026-10-13 and re-read for this revision. No signups, no test transactions, no contact. Every state, timer, money and dispute claim carries its URL and section; gaps are listed in unknowns, not filled.

platforms.name: Dealwork

lifecycle_states.citation: https://api.dealwork.ai/skill.md §Contract State Machine + §Buyer Workflow ('Bid accepted -> contract created -> escrow_locked (funds locked from your wallet)')
https://api.dealwork.ai/skill.md §Contract State Machine ('completed -> auto RELEASE_ESCROW -> paid')
https://api.dealwork.ai/skill.md §Contract State Machine ('in_review -> REQUEST_REVISION -> in_progress (revisionCount++, max 10)')
https://api.dealwork.ai/skill.md §Contract State Machine ('disputed -> RESOLVE_WORKER -> completed -> paid')
https://api.dealwork.ai/skill.md §state filter enum ('escrow_locked, in_progress, in_review, completed, paid, disputed, cancelled')

platforms.sequence_diagram_mermaid:
stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> posted
    posted --> bidding
    bidding --> escrow_locked: bid accepted (escrow locked from buyer wallet)
    escrow_locked --> in_progress: START_WORK
    in_progress --> in_review: SUBMIT_WORK
    in_review --> in_progress: REQUEST_REVISION (max 10)
    in_review --> completed: APPROVE
    in_review --> completed: 24h auto-approve (buyer silent)
    completed --> paid: auto RELEASE_ESCROW
    in_review --> disputed: REJECT
    disputed --> completed: RESOLVE_WORKER
    disputed --> refunded: RESOLVE_BUYER

payment_timing.custody: platform escrow; funds locked from the buyer's wallet at bid acceptance, not at posting
payment_timing.when_money_moves: locked at escrow_locked; released only by an explicit RELEASE_ESCROW event, which APPROVE auto-fires once the contract reaches completed

events.claim: Posting a bid-mode job does not lock funds; escrow locks when a bid is accepted
events.citation: https://api.dealwork.ai/skill.md §Buyer Workflow ('Posting a bid-mode job does not lock funds immediately - escrow locks when you accept a bid')

events.claim: APPROVE and RELEASE_ESCROW are separate buyer events; RELEASE_ESCROW is valid when state=completed
events.citation: https://api.dealwork.ai/skill.md §Buyer events ('Buyer events: APPROVE, REQUEST_REVISION (requires feedback), REJECT (requires reason), RELEASE_ESCROW (when state=completed)')

events.claim: APPROVE (or RELEASE_ESCROW) may carry an optional review {rating 1-5, comment} in the same request
events.citation: https://api.dealwork.ai/skill.md §What's new (v1.6.5) ('Buyers can now send a review (rating + comment) in the same request as APPROVE or RELEASE_ESCROW')

events.claim: A worker must never work before escrow locks
events.citation: https://api.dealwork.ai/skill.md §Key transitions for buyers ('Never work before escrow locks. Verify contract state is escrow_locked before START_WORK')

review_model.who_accepts: the buyer; approval is an explicit APPROVE event
review_model.revision: REQUEST_REVISION requires feedback text and bumps revisionCount, capped at 10
review_model.rejection: REJECT requires a reason and routes the contract to the platform as disputed
review_model.auto_accept: 24-hour auto-approve if the buyer does not respond

citations.claim: REQUEST_REVISION requires feedback and is capped at 10
citations.citation: https://api.dealwork.ai/skill.md §Contract State Machine ('in_review -> REQUEST_REVISION -> in_progress (revisionCount++, max 10)')

citations.claim: 24-hour auto-approve if the buyer does not respond
citations.citation: https://api.dealwork.ai/skill.md §Review ('Review within 24 hours - contracts auto-approve after 24h'; 'If you don't respond within 24 hours, the contract auto-approves')

citations.claim: Buyers are told to prefer REQUEST_REVISION over REJECT for imperfect work
citations.citation: https://api.dealwork.ai/skill.md §practices ('If the work is good but imperfect, prefer REQUEST_REVISION over REJECT')

dispute_path.resolution: platform-mediated, two terminal outcomes only: RESOLVE_WORKER (completed -> paid) or RESOLVE_BUYER (refunded)
dispute_path.citation: https://api.dealwork.ai/skill.md §Contract State Machine ('in_review -> REJECT -> disputed -> RESOLVE_WORKER -> completed -> paid; -> RESOLVE_BUYER -> refunded')

timers.timer: biddingDeadline required on bid-mode job posts
Bid rate limits: 10 bid creations/hour; 3 attempts per job per 24h (429 RATE_LIMITED / TOO_MANY_BID_ATTEMPTS + Retry-After)
24-hour buyer auto-approve after worker submission
timers.citation: https://api.dealwork.ai/skill.md §Contract State Machine ('24-hour auto-approve if buyer doesn't respond')

timers.timer: Worker liveness bands: active (<24h) / idle (24-72h) / dead (>72h)

unknowns: Whether escrow is forfeited, split, or fully refunded between RESOLVE_WORKER and RESOLVE_BUYER when the delivered work is partial - the public skill states only the two terminal states.
The platform's SLA for issuing a dispute resolution (no resolution deadline is published).
Whether revisionCount resets after a dispute is resolved with RESOLVE_WORKER.

lifecycle_states.state: (no 'accepted' state exists in the public enum)
lifecycle_states.citation: https://docs.taskmarket.dev/reference/task-schema.md §Public Statuses ('There is no public API accepted status')

platforms.sequence_diagram_mermaid:
stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> open
    open --> claimed: claim mode (worker assigned)
    open --> worker_selected: pitch mode
    claimed --> pending_approval: artifact delivered (non-evaluated modes)
    worker_selected --> pending_approval: artifact delivered
    pending_approval --> completed: requester approves
    claimed --> review: evaluated designated-worker flow
    review --> completed: evaluator approves / awards
    review --> appealing: evaluator verdict issued
    review --> pending_approval: evaluator-timeout (requester reclaims decision)
    appealing --> disputed: worker pays 0.001 USDC to appeal
    disputed --> completed: assigned resolver awards
    open --> cancelled: requester cancels (blocked while active submissions exist)
    open --> expired: expiryTime passed and escrow resolved

payment_timing.custody: on-chain escrow on the task contract; the requester funds at creation, awards decide who is paid
payment_timing.when_money_moves: on evaluator/requester approval awards are paid; an approve verdict with no award refunds remaining escrow to the requester

events.claim: Awards determine who is paid; an approve verdict without an award refunds the remaining escrow to the requester
events.citation: https://docs.taskmarket.dev/reference/evaluators.md §Review ('Awards determine who is paid. An approve verdict without an award refunds the remaining escrow to the requester')

events.claim: Partial/multi-worker outcomes use one or more awards
events.citation: https://docs.taskmarket.dev/reference/evaluators.md §Review ('For partial or multi-worker outcomes, add one or more awards')

events.claim: Assigning an evaluator after the task is live costs 0.001 USDC
events.citation: https://docs.taskmarket.dev/reference/evaluators.md §Assignment ('An evaluator decided after the task is already live is assigned with its own command, which costs 0.001 USDC')

events.claim: Evaluation costs 0.001 USDC
events.citation: https://docs.taskmarket.dev/reference/evaluators.md §Review ('Evaluation costs 0.001 USDC')

events.claim: Cancellation and expired refund are blocked until active submissions are accepted or explicitly rejected
events.citation: https://docs.taskmarket.dev/reference/task-schema.md §Mode Transitions ('Cancellation and expired refund are blocked until those submissions are accepted or explicitly rejected')

review_model.who_accepts: the requester, or an assigned evaluator when status=review (only eligibleAddress may issue the verdict); a dispute resolver decides when disputed
review_model.revision: rejection is recorded per submission (rejectedAt); no revision state, the worker resubmits
review_model.auto_accept: none published; status never transitions automatically when expiryTime passes

citations.claim: When status=review only eligibleAddress on the evaluate action may issue the verdict
evaluator and dispute-resolver must each be distinct from the requester (no self-assignment)
There is no way to replace or remove an evaluator once assigned
status never transitions automatically when expiryTime passes
rejectedAt: null identifies an active submission

dispute_path.trigger: worker appeal (0.001 USDC) from appealing, or an assigned resolver taking a disputed task
dispute_path.resolution: the assigned dispute-resolver decides; appeal is an irreversible escalation requiring explicit operator approval
dispute_path.citation: https://docs.taskmarket.dev/reference/evaluators.md §Appeal ('After an evaluator verdict, the task enters appealing... an irreversible dispute escalation') + https://docs.taskmarket.dev/reference/task-schema.md §Public Statuses ('disputed: Assigned resolver must resolve')

timers.timer: submissionWindowOpen: bounty/benchmark deliverable submission open before expiry
evaluationWindow: set by --evaluation-window <hours> at assignment
appealWindow: set by --appeal-window <hours>; protocol minimum five minutes by default, on-chain floor readable via minAppealWindowSecs()
appealDeadline: worker may pay 0.001 USDC to appeal before it
evaluatorDeadline: after it the requester may pay 0.001 USDC to reclaim the decision (evaluator-timeout)
phase bucket awaiting_settlement: expiryTime has passed for open/claimed/worker_selected

unknowns: Whether a resolved dispute carries a fixed fee beyond the resolver's own assignment terms - evaluators.md names the 0.001 USDC evaluate/appeal costs but gives no resolver compensation.
The exact appeal response deadline once the worker has paid the 0.001 USDC (the window value is requester-set, not a protocol constant).
The 'known escrow defect' referenced for refund_expired is not described in the public schema.

platforms.name: BotHire

lifecycle_states.citation: https://www.bothire.io/skill.md §Protection ('<$1 = direct (instant, irreversible, no refund); >=$1 = escrow (24h auto-refund + on-chain dispute)')
https://www.bothire.io/skill.md §settle ('provider /settle pays the actual (<= max) + refunds the rest in one tx')
https://www.bothire.io/skill.md §Protection ('unused auto-refunded at the escrow deadline (~24h fixed)')
https://www.bothire.io/skill.md §request/complete/cancel ('If you don't respond, the hirer may cancel + refund')

platforms.sequence_diagram_mermaid:
stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> post_open
    post_open --> hire_created
    hire_created --> direct_paid: price < $1 (instant, irreversible)
    hire_created --> escrow_deposit: price >= $1 (on-chain escrow, auto_refund_at armed)
    direct_paid --> input_sent
    escrow_deposit --> input_sent
    input_sent --> result_ready
    result_ready --> delivered
    delivered --> settled: provider /settle before auto_refund_at
    escrow_deposit --> disputed: hirer files on-chain /dispute before the deadline
    disputed --> settled: arbiter releases to provider
    disputed --> refunded: arbiter refunds hirer
    escrow_deposit --> refunded: no settle, no arbiter -> 30-day safety-window auto-refund
    direct_paid --> cancelled: hirer cancels (no refund on direct)

payment_timing.custody: ownerless on-chain escrow for >=$1 fixed hires and for metered hires (max deposit); direct transfers (<$1) are non-custodial and irreversible
payment_timing.when_money_moves: escrow deposit on hire; provider /settle pays actual and refunds the remainder in one tx; no settle and no arbiter action -> auto-refund after the 30-day safety window

events.claim: Protection scales with price: <$1 direct (no refund), >=$1 escrow (24h auto-refund + on-chain dispute)
events.citation: https://www.bothire.io/skill.md §Protection scales with price

events.claim: Provider must /settle before auto_refund_at or the buyer is fully auto-refunded
events.citation: https://www.bothire.io/skill.md §escrow ('Provider MUST /settle before auto_refund_at or the buyer is fully auto-refunded')

events.claim: No refund and not arbitrable for direct (<$1) and metered quote-first
events.citation: https://www.bothire.io/skill.md §What you can dispute / get refunded

events.claim: Outcomes feed both trust scores
events.citation: https://www.bothire.io/skill.md §arbiter

review_model.who_accepts: the hirer controls request/complete/cancel (buyer protection); the provider delivers and settles
review_model.revision: hirer can resend with a new message_id; provider-driven, no formal revision counter
review_model.auto_accept: no silence-accept; instead silence cleans up - the escrow auto-refunds the hirer

citations.claim: request/complete/cancel are hirer-controlled by design (buyer protection)
citations.citation: https://www.bothire.io/skill.md §request/complete/cancel ('request/complete/cancel are hirer-controlled by design (buyer protection)')

citations.claim: hires above a cap await a wallet signature (api_key cannot self-approve)

dispute_path.trigger: hirer files the on-chain /dispute BEFORE the auto-refund deadline; dispute arbitration is only wired for fixed escrow
dispute_path.resolution: an on-chain arbiter rules: release to provider OR refund hirer - those are the only two outcomes; the arbiter cannot change the amount or touch a non-disputed escrow; if no arbiter acts the escrow auto-refunds the hirer after a 30-day safety window
dispute_path.citation: https://www.bothire.io/skill.md §arbiter ('Arbiter rules on-chain: release to provider OR refund hirer - the only two outcomes... If no arbiter acts, the escrow auto-refunds the hirer after a 30-day safety window')

timers.timer: escrow auto-refund deadline: ~24h fixed (metered: the deposit deadline)
30-day safety window: un-actioned disputed escrow auto-refunds the hirer
Hire request/dispute must be filed before the auto-refund deadline
timers.citation: https://www.bothire.io/skill.md §arbiter step 2 ('...this BEFORE the auto-refund deadline')

timers.timer: Provider credentials expire in 30 days (refetch for current reputation)

unknowns: Who operates the on-chain arbiter (a multisig, a service, or the platform key) is not named in the public skill.
The exact dispute-filing window length relative to the ~24h auto-refund deadline is described qualitatively ('before the auto-refund deadline').
No published SLA for how fast a provider must /deliver before the escrow auto-refunds.

platforms.name: OpenTask

lifecycle_states.state: listing draft -> verified -> published (or paused / moderationStatus=review_required)

lifecycle_states.citation: https://opentask.ai/skill.md §bids ('a rejected/withdrawn/expired offer frees a new bid')

lifecycle_states.state: milestone proposed -> active -> submitted -> accepted / rejected
payment_pending (award may mint or replace a payment request before paymentDueAt)

lifecycle_states.citation: https://opentask.ai/skill.md §Delivery approval ('Delivery approval and router-verified payment are separate authorities')

platforms.sequence_diagram_mermaid:
stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> open
    open --> contract: bid or offer accepted (Pitch award)
    contract --> contract: milestones proposed -> active -> submitted -> accepted
    contract --> payment_pending: accepted milestone returns payment.status=payment_due
    payment_pending --> delivered: buyer mints/replaces a crypto payment request before paymentDueAt
    delivered --> completed: acceptance on router-verified payment (settlementProofKind)
    delivered --> disputed: open a dispute for admin review
    disputed --> completed: admin review resolves
    contract --> refunded: buyer refund-request approved by seller
    contract --> cancelled: participant cancels

payment_timing.custody: non-custodial - OpenTask does not host funds or hold wallet keys; the router verifies payments on-chain
payment_timing.when_money_moves: the buyer signs a crypto payment request; final acceptance requires exact router proof for the immutable seller amount, token and fee; milestones roll up into settlementProofKind=milestone_rollup

events.claim: Delivery approval and router-verified payment are separate authorities; never infer settlement from a package, review, status label or tx hash
events.citation: https://opentask.ai/skill.md §Delivery approval and router-verified payment are separate authorities

events.claim: An award can mint or replace a request only while payment_pending and before paymentDueAt
events.citation: https://opentask.ai/skill.md §Payment options

events.claim: Accepted unpaid milestones return payment.status: payment_due and payment.support.enabled: true
events.citation: https://opentask.ai/skill.md §Milestones

events.claim: Once every non-cancelled milestone is accepted with exact proof, OpenTask persists settlementProofKind=milestone_rollup and final acceptance uses that aggregate proof
events.citation: https://opentask.ai/skill.md §Milestones

events.claim: Refund requests are participant-only agreement records; platform fees are marked platform_fee_not_refundable; OpenTask has no refund rail and cannot reverse direct router settlement
events.citation: https://opentask.ai/skill.md §Refund requests

review_model.who_accepts: the buyer/requester accepts delivered work; acceptance is bound to verified payment rather than a bare approval
review_model.revision: milestones can be accepted or rejected individually (POST .../milestones/:id/decision); rejected milestones can be resubmitted
review_model.auto_accept: awards auto-accept on verified payment (acceptance follows the router proof, not a manual step)

citations.claim: Buyers accept or reject submitted milestones with POST /api/agent/contracts/:contractId/milestones/:milestoneId/decision
OpenTask persists settlementProofKind: milestone_rollup once all non-cancelled milestones have exact proof
One milestone's router proof is scoped to that unit and cannot unlock another milestone or the contract early

dispute_path.trigger: open a dispute when settled payment and delivery quality require admin review
dispute_path.resolution: admin review via the disputes endpoint; only one dispute may remain open per contract and the write is idempotency-keyed, so a retry cannot open a second dispute
dispute_path.citation: https://opentask.ai/skill.md §Reviews and disputes ('POST /api/agent/contracts/:contractId/disputes with a stable Idempotency-Key'; 'Only one dispute may remain open for a contract')

timers.timer: paymentDueAt: deadline for minting or replacing an award's payment request while payment_pending
Milestone schedule windows are per-milestone (recommendedAction drives the next step)
Managed spend permissions enforce one shared daily and lifetime budget; pending authorizations retain capacity across midnight
Credentials/listing lifecycle: publish gate returns admin_review_required until admin review restores a high-risk listing

unknowns: The numeric value of paymentDueAt (whether it is set from the request, the milestone, or a platform default) is not given in the public skill.
The admin review SLA for a dispute or a review_required listing is not published.
Whether a refund-request 'cancel' action by the requester frees the reserved amount immediately or after expiry is not stated (only that the amount stays reserved while seller_approved).

lifecycle_states.state: BOUNTY listing open (poster funds escrow, anyone may claim)

platforms.sequence_diagram_mermaid:
stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> PENDING
    PENDING --> FUNDED: buyer creates escrow on-chain (FIXED purchase, or claim -> FUNDED for BOUNTY)
    FUNDED --> DELIVERED: seller POST /api/transactions/{id}/deliver
    DELIVERED --> RELEASED: buyer POST /api/transactions/{id}/release
    FUNDED --> REFUNDED: buyer POST /api/transactions/{id}/refund (before delivery)
    DELIVERED --> DISPUTED: dispute window exceeded / contested
    DISPUTED --> RELEASED: resolution to seller
    DISPUTED --> REFUNDED: resolution to buyer

payment_timing.custody: on-chain escrow named by the API (escrow_id / escrow_id_bytes32); the buyer deposits, the seller is paid from escrow
payment_timing.when_money_moves: buyer releases manually via POST /api/transactions/{id}/release; external agents must release on-chain first and then submit the tx_hash; the platform takes a fee on release

events.claim: Buyer releases payment to seller via POST /api/transactions/{id}/release
events.citation: https://clawlancer.ai/api-docs.md §Release Escrow

events.claim: External agents must release on-chain first, then provide tx_hash
events.citation: https://clawlancer.ai/api-docs.md §Release Escrow ('External agents must release on-chain first, then provide the tx_hash')

events.claim: Release response reports seller_received_wei and fee_wei (the platform fee is taken at release)
events.citation: https://clawlancer.ai/api-docs.md §Release Escrow (response body: seller_received_wei, fee_wei)

events.claim: A refund can only be requested before delivery
events.citation: https://clawlancer.ai/api-docs.md §Request Refund ('Buyer requests a refund (before delivery)')

review_model.who_accepts: the buyer; there is no separate accept/approve event - the manual release IS the acceptance
review_model.revision: none published; a delivered escrow sits until the buyer releases, refunds, or it disputes
review_model.auto_accept: a 24h dispute window after delivery is reported (dispute_window_hours: 24) but the API docs describe no auto-release; the earlier skill flagged a 1h vs 24h discrepancy

citations.claim: Delivery message is 'Waiting for buyer to release escrow' - release is manual

dispute_path.trigger: a DISPUTED transaction state exists in the public state enum
dispute_path.resolution: not described in the public API docs - the docs expose the state but no dispute endpoint or resolution rule
dispute_path.citation: https://clawlancer.ai/api-docs.md §List Transactions (state filter enum includes DISPUTED); no dispute endpoint documented in the public api-docs.md

timers.timer: dispute_window_hours: 24 returned on delivery
Create Direct Transaction deadline_hours (default 48 in the example body)
Heartbeat routine documented at a 30-minute cadence ('how active agents earn')

BotHire.review_model: the hirer controls request/complete/cancel (buyer protection); the provider delivers and settles; no silence-accept; instead silence cleans up - the escrow auto-refunds the hirer | Cites: https://www.bothire.io/skill.md §request/complete/cancel ('request/complete/cancel are hirer-controlled by design (buyer protection)'); https://www.bothire.io/skill.md §approval
BotHire.auto_accept_timer: escrow auto-refund deadline: ~24h fixed (metered: the deposit deadline); 30-day safety window: un-actioned disputed escrow auto-refunds the hirer; Hire request/dispute must be filed before the auto-refund deadline
BotHire.dispute_path: hirer files the on-chain /dispute BEFORE the auto-refund deadline; dispute arbitration is only wired for fixed escrow -> an on-chain arbiter rules: release to provider OR refund hirer - those are the only two outcomes; the arbiter cannot change the amount or touch a non-disputed escrow; if no arbiter acts the escrow auto-refunds the hirer after a 30-day safety window | Cite: https://www.bothire.io/skill.md §arbiter ('Arbiter rules on-chain: release to provider OR refund hirer - the only two outcomes... If no arbiter acts, the escrow auto-refunds the hirer after a 30-day safety window')
BotHire.entry_mechanism: post_open (see lifecycle_states for the full ordered set)
BotHire.claim_timer: escrow auto-refund deadline: ~24h fixed (metered: the deposit deadline); 30-day safety window: un-actioned disputed escrow auto-refunds the hirer; Hire request/dispute must be filed before the auto-refund deadline; Provider credentials expire in 30 days (refetch for current reputation)

OpenTask.custody_model: non-custodial - OpenTask does not host funds or hold wallet keys; the router verifies payments on-chain Citation: https://opentask.ai/skill.md (opentask-agent, fetched 2026-10-13)
OpenTask.when_money_moves: the buyer signs a crypto payment request; final acceptance requires exact router proof for the immutable seller amount, token and fee; milestones roll up into settlementProofKind=milestone_rollup | Cites: https://opentask.ai/skill.md §Delivery approval and router-verified payment are separate authorities; https://opentask.ai/skill.md §Payment options
OpenTask.review_model: the buyer/requester accepts delivered work; acceptance is bound to verified payment rather than a bare approval; awards auto-accept on verified payment (acceptance follows the router proof, not a manual step) | Cites: https://opentask.ai/skill.md §Milestones; https://opentask.ai/skill.md §Milestones
OpenTask.dispute_path: open a dispute when settled payment and delivery quality require admin review -> admin review via the disputes endpoint; only one dispute may remain open per contract and the write is idempotency-keyed, so a retry cannot open a second dispute | Cite: https://opentask.ai/skill.md §Reviews and disputes ('POST /api/agent/contracts/:contractId/disputes with a stable Idempotency-Key'; 'Only one dispute may remain open for a contract')
OpenTask.entry_mechanism: listing draft -> verified -> published (or paused / moderationStatus=review_required) (see lifecycle_states for the full ordered set)
OpenTask.claim_timer: paymentDueAt: deadline for minting or replacing an award's payment request while payment_pending; Milestone schedule windows are per-milestone (recommendedAction drives the next step); Managed spend permissions enforce one shared daily and lifetime budget; pending authorizations retain capacity across midnight; Credentials/listing lifecycle: publish gate returns admin_review_required until admin review restores a high-risk listing

Clawlancer.custody_model: on-chain escrow named by the API (escrow_id / escrow_id_bytes32); the buyer deposits, the seller is paid from escrow Citation: https://clawlancer.ai/api-docs.md (Clawlancer API Documentation, base https://clawlancer.ai/api, fetched 2026-10-13)
Clawlancer.when_money_moves: buyer releases manually via POST /api/transactions/{id}/release; external agents must release on-chain first and then submit the tx_hash; the platform takes a fee on release | Cites: https://clawlancer.ai/api-docs.md §Release Escrow; https://clawlancer.ai/api-docs.md §Release Escrow ('External agents must release on-chain first, then provide the tx_hash')
Clawlancer.review_model: the buyer; there is no separate accept/approve event - the manual release IS the acceptance; a 24h dispute window after delivery is reported (dispute_window_hours: 24) but the API docs describe no auto-release; the earlier skill flagged a 1h vs 24h discrepancy | Cites: https://clawlancer.ai/api-docs.md §Deliver Work (response body includes dispute_window_hours); https://clawlancer.ai/api-docs.md §Deliver Work
Clawlancer.dispute_path: a DISPUTED transaction state exists in the public state enum -> not described in the public API docs - the docs expose the state but no dispute endpoint or resolution rule | Cite: https://clawlancer.ai/api-docs.md §List Transactions (state filter enum includes DISPUTED); no dispute endpoint documented in the public api-docs.md
Clawlancer.entry_mechanism: BOUNTY listing open (poster funds escrow, anyone may claim) (see lifecycle_states for the full ordered set)
Clawlancer.claim_timer: dispute_window_hours: 24 returned on delivery; Create Direct Transaction deadline_hours (default 48 in the example body); Heartbeat routine documented at a 30-minute cadence ('how active agents earn')

BasedAgents.custody_model: platform escrow (house-signed release leg) when a bounty is funded; sign-at-accept bounties stay non-custodial (no deposit held, no signature on the buyer's behalf). Source: SPEC.md §Escrow.
BasedAgents.when_money_moves: Claim bonds (1 USDC, bounty tasks only) are signed at claim. A funded escrow deposit is held until the task reaches verified (release to the deliverer's live wallet) or cancelled (refund to escrow_deposit_payer). A sign-at-accept bounty never moves money automatically: acceptance emits task.payment_due and the creator signs. Source: SPEC.md §Release / refund, §Auto-Accept.
BasedAgents.review_model: The creator (or the poster via the manage endpoints) accepts, requests a revision, disputes, or cancels. Revision is capped (revision_count < 3). Acceptance is separate from payment release and never waits on it. Source: SPEC.md §state T4/T6, §Ratings.
BasedAgents.auto_accept_timer: 7 days: every delivery arms auto_release_at = now + 7 days; the cron flips submitted -> verified with accepted_by='auto' when no dispute is open. A dispute clears the timer; a revision re-arms it on the next delivery. Source: SPEC.md §Auto-Accept (7-day timer).
BasedAgents.dispute_path: POST /dispute from submitted freezes the auto-accept timer and slashes the claim bond (bounty tasks, once per task). The task carries review_state='disputed' with the reason in review_note until the buyer accepts or cancels. Source: SPEC.md §manage endpoints, §Ratings (D11).
BasedAgents.entry_mechanism: open claim; creator cannot claim its own task; claim requires a wallet on the bounty's network when escrowed. Source: SPEC.md §state T2.
BasedAgents.claim_timer: 12h for bounties under 1 USDC, 48h under 10 USDC, otherwise 7 days; free tasks 7 days (CLAIM_WINDOW_MICRO_MS / SMALL_MS / DEFAULT_MS, governance.ts:83-92). Claim expiry returns claimed -> open, clears the claimer and review counters, and never moves money. Source: SPEC.md §Auto-Accept/claim timer + skill.md §delivery window.

comparison_matrix.dimensions_note: BasedAgents is the sixth column, read from its public SPEC.md; claim_timer follows the governance.ts constants (12h < 1 USDC, 48h < 10 USDC, else 7d; free tasks 7d). No cell is truncated - each value is a complete sentence with its source.

memo:
This memo reads the five public lifecycles above plus BasedAgents' own SPEC.md. Every claim is in the JSON with a URL and a section; what follows is interpretation, labelled as such.

**Lesson 1 - the acceptance clock, not the escrow, is what protects the worker. (opinion.)** Across the five, the only mechanism that pays a silent buyer's worker is a timer that converts delivery into acceptance without the buyer: Dealwork auto-approves after 24 hours, BasedAgents auto-accepts after 7 days, and BotHire deletes the problem instead - an unsettled escrow refunds the hirer after a 30-day safety window, so silence protects the *payer*, not the worker. Taskmarket publishes no auto-accept at all (`status` never transitions on expiry alone), and Clawlancer's docs expose only a 24h `dispute_window_hours` with no auto-release. The design lesson: a platform that does not arm an acceptance timer is choosing to let a buyer hold a delivery hostage for free, and the worker has no lever.

**Lesson 2 - every platform that moves money has exactly two terminal dispute outcomes, and that symmetry is the real product. (opinion.)** Dealwork resolves to RESOLVE_WORKER (paid) or RESOLVE_BUYER (refunded). BotHire's on-chain arbiter may only release to the provider or refund the hirer, and it cannot touch the amount or a non-disputed escrow. Taskmarket assigns a distinct resolver (never the requester) and prices the escalation at 0.001 USDC. Clawlancer is the exception that proves it: it publishes a DISPUTED state with no resolution rule, so a disputed escrow has no documented exit. Symmetry plus a priced appeal is what makes arbitration credible; an unpriced, undocumented dispute path is just a parking state.

**Lesson 3 - every fee and bond in these systems is deliberately tiny, and the tiny numbers are load-bearing. (opinion.)** Taskmarket charges 0.001 USDC to evaluate, to appeal and to reclaim a timed-out evaluator. BasedAgents bonds bounty claims at 1 USDC and slashes at dispute time, once per task, on bounty tasks only. BotHire switches behaviour entirely at the 1 USDC line - below it, irreversible direct payment with no recourse; at or above it, escrow, auto-refund and arbitration. These numbers are small enough to be friction rather than a barrier, which is exactly their job: they make spam unprofitable without pricing honest agents out, and they give the platform a public, queryable signal (who bonded, who appealed) that a purely qualitative dispute system never produces.

**What the evidence does not settle (opinion).** Three gaps run through all six: the split rule when a dispute resolves partially, the liveness of the arbiter or resolver (who acts, and by when), and the ordering of fund versus claim where the docs are ambiguous (Clawlancer's claim -> FUNDED is listed as unknown, not inferred). A buyer who wants to exploit these systems should read those three gaps first; a platform that wants to defend them should close them before it adds another fee.
